title: Cricket Australia Approves Big Bash Privatization; Melbourne Renegades Sale to Launch
dek: Cricket Australia approved privatization of the Big Bash League, moving forward with a sales process for the Melbourne Renegades with a target date of the 2027-28 season for new ownership. The decision passed despite opposition from New South Wales and Queensland.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Australia adopted a self-determination model allowing individual states to choose whether and when to sell stakes in their franchises, retreating from an earlier proposal for league-wide privatization.
bottom_line: The franchise ownership question now rests with individual states rather than a centralized mandate. The Renegades sale will be the first test of whether private investors see the Big Bash as a viable acquisition, and the outcome will determine whether other clubs follow into the market.
body: Cricket Australia approved privatization of the Big Bash League, according to reporting from the Guardian and BBC Sport. The decision launches a sales process for the Melbourne Renegades with the aim of new ownership by the 2027-28 season. The Renegades will operate in caretaker mode, managed by Cricket Australia, during the coming 2026-27 season before being sold and rebranded.

The approval came months after Cricket Victoria controversially proposed merging the Melbourne Stars and Melbourne Renegades. NSW and Queensland were fiercely opposed to privatization, while Tasmania, Victoria, and Western Australia have long supported it. Rather than proceed with league-wide privatization as initially proposed, Cricket Australia adopted a self-determination model, per BBC Sport, allowing individual states to have the final say on whether and when to sell stakes in their franchises. The retreat from full privatization signals that internal resistance was too strong to pass a uniform model.

Cricket Australia will retain control over international scheduling, player availability, salary caps, and media rights. The body also holds approval power over potential investors and will set a reserve price for the Renegades sale. Cricket Victoria will continue to manage the Stars, though that franchise will likely be renamed after the Renegades are sold. CA will consider allowing other clubs to go to market depending on how well the Renegades sale proceeds.

The decision follows England's profitable model: the ECB's sale of stakes in The Hundred's eight teams generated more than 500 million pounds, with the franchises collectively valued at more than 975 million pounds, per BBC Sport. BBC Sport reports that officials from Cricket Australia met with some owners of Hundred franchises this summer, and a number have expressed interest in investing in the Big Bash. According to BBC Sport, Hobart Hurricanes, Melbourne Stars, and Perth Scorchers are reportedly keen to bring in private investment. The two Sydney-based sides, Sixers and Thunder, along with Brisbane Heat and Adelaide Strikers, are reportedly reluctant to commit to private investment.

The Renegades sale will not affect the 2026-27 BBL or WBBL seasons. Perth Scorchers won the men's Big Bash in 2026, their sixth title. Cricket Australia is continuing constructive discussions with the Australian Cricketers' Association over an ongoing pay dispute. The upcoming BBL gets underway on December 12 when the Renegades and Scorchers play a historic match in Chennai.
